headline: March CPI accelerates to +2.4% YoY as Hormuz-driven gasoline surge (+21.2% M/M) reverses six months of disinflation; BoC faces April 29 decision with bond markets pricing potential hikes
headline_rationale: The March CPI print (+2.4%, up 0.6pp from February's +1.8%) represents the sharpest monthly acceleration since mid-2022, driven by the largest monthly gasoline price increase on record (+21.2% M/M). This directly precedes the April 29 BoC decision with Monetary Policy Report and the April 28 Federal Spring Economic Update — the two most consequential scheduled events this week. Bond markets have shifted from pricing cuts to pricing ~41bps of tightening by year-end, a material reversal in rate expectations that affects financing costs for $1,161.7B in tracked pipeline projects.

top_stories.story: March CPI acceleration to +2.4% driven by record gasoline surge
top_stories.facts: Headline CPI rose to +2.4% YoY from +1.8% in February. Gasoline prices surged +21.2% M/M, the largest monthly increase on record, driven by Strait of Hormuz disruptions. CPI ex-gasoline was +2.2% YoY, down from +2.4% ex-gasoline in February. Food purchased from stores rose +4.4% YoY; fresh vegetables +7.8% YoY.

top_stories.story: Strait of Hormuz volatility: ceasefire, reopening, re-closure reports
top_stories.facts: Ceasefire agreed April 8; Strait reopened April 17; re-closure reports drove WTI back to $86.25. Tanker traffic had dropped to near-zero during blockade. WTI collapsed from ~$128 peak (Apr 2) to $83.85 (Apr 17), a ~34% decline in 15 days, then rebounded. Brent at $95.42. OPEC+ output fell 9.4 mb/d M/M to 42.4 mb/d.

top_stories.story: BoC April 29 decision and Federal Spring Economic Update April 28
top_stories.facts: BoC held at 2.25% (7th consecutive hold). April 29 decision accompanied by Monetary Policy Report. Bond markets price ~92% probability of hold but ~41bps of tightening by year-end. 2-year yields up 35bps; yield curve bear flattening. Federal Spring Economic Update scheduled April 28; previous projection showed $78.3B deficit.

top_stories.story: Trade deficit widens to $5.7B as imports hit record $72.1B
top_stories.facts: Merchandise trade deficit widened to $5.7B in February from revised $4.2B in January. Exports +6.4% to $66.3B; imports +8.4% to record $72.1B. Export gains led by motor vehicles/parts (+24.2%), precious metals (+14.2%). Exports to non-U.S. economies +17% YoY; to U.S. -10% YoY (trade diversion).

top_stories.story: Consumer confidence at 11-month low; wage growth accelerates to +4.7%
top_stories.facts: Bloomberg-Nanos Consumer Confidence Index fell to 46.93, an 11-month low. Expectations sub-index lost ~10 points over 4 weeks. Only 15% see stronger economy in 6 months (down from 27%). Meanwhile, average hourly wages rose +4.7% YoY to $37.73/hr, fastest since Oct 2024.

data_driven_callouts: CPI acceleration to +2.4% affects financing cost assumptions for 4,471 active projects (Proposed + Under Review + Approved) representing the bulk of $1,161.7B pipeline value. Bond market pricing of ~41bps year-end tightening, if realized, would raise borrowing costs for projects not yet at financial close.

The pipeline tracks 550 power/energy projects ($490.9B) and 39 oil/gas projects ($97.3B) with direct exposure to Hormuz-driven commodity price volatility. WTI at $86.25 is above breakeven for most tracked Alberta oil sands projects.

Housing starts at 235,852 SAAR against CMHC's 430,000-480,000/yr affordability target leaves a structural gap. The pipeline tracks 166 residential projects ($31.9B) and 1,032 infrastructure projects ($135.4B) that include transit and water/wastewater enabling housing development.

Manufacturing sales rebounded +3.6% to $71.2B with unfilled orders at record $117.6B; the pipeline tracks 45 manufacturing projects ($67.3B). Construction and manufacturing sectors report highest hiring difficulty at 49.5% and 47.4% respectively.

Trade diversion from U.S. (-10% YoY) toward non-U.S. markets (+17% YoY) coincides with Canada-China trade engagement; 69 transport/logistics projects ($27.3B) and port/logistics facilities have exposure to shifting trade corridors.

global_context.development: Strait of Hormuz crisis and oil supply disruption
global_context.details: Largest disruption to world energy supply since the 1970s. ~25% of seaborne oil and 20% of LNG transited the Strait. Ceasefire Apr 8, reopening Apr 17, re-closure reports emerging. OPEC+ output fell 9.4 mb/d.
global_context.canadian_connection: Canada is the only G7 nation without a strategic petroleum reserve. TMX provides an alternative corridor for Asian buyers. 550 power/energy and 39 oil/gas projects ($588.2B) have direct commodity exposure.

global_context.details: Canada announced 6-month pause on retaliatory tariffs for U.S. goods in manufacturing, food/beverage, health care, and national security (Apr 15). U.S. restructured Section 232: 50% on aluminum, steel, copper. CUSMA joint review scheduled July 2026.
global_context.canadian_connection: Merchandise exports to U.S. -10% YoY vs. non-U.S. +17% YoY — active trade diversion. Manufacturing sector reports 47.4% hiring difficulty. 45 manufacturing projects ($67.3B) tracked.

global_context.development: U.S. Federal Reserve holds at 3.50%-3.75%; April 29 decision pending
global_context.details: Fed held for 2nd consecutive meeting. March FOMC minutes showed willingness to consider rate increases. U.S. consumer sentiment plunged to 50.8 (second-lowest since 1952). Nonfarm payrolls +178,000; unemployment 4.3%.
global_context.canadian_connection: BoC-Fed rate differential affects CAD and capital flows. Both central banks decide April 29. Canada-U.S. rate spread influences cross-border investment in tracked projects.

global_context.development: China Q1 GDP +5.0% beats expectations; Canada-China trade engagement deepens
global_context.details: China Q1 GDP +5.0% YoY (beat 4.8% forecast). Industrial production +6.1%. March imports +27.8% YoY (strongest since Nov 2021). EV/battery/wind exports surged 78%/50%/45%.
global_context.canadian_connection: Bilateral trade C$124.8B in 2025. Minister Sidhu at consumer expo; Finance Minister Champagne advanced trade partnerships. TMX enables independent supply corridor to China. Mining projects ($146B) have exposure to Chinese demand.

global_context.development: ECB holds at 2.15%; global monetary tightening cycle re-emerging
global_context.details: ECB main rate 2.15%, deposit facility 2.0%. Markets pricing hold April 29-30, hike in June. Traders expect at least 2.5% by year-end. Global central banks shifting from easing to inflation response.
global_context.canadian_connection: Synchronized global rate pressure affects Canadian capital costs and commodity pricing. BoC, Fed, and ECB all deciding within April 29-30 window.
